one_fix: Move the whole 'The scan record' block (H2 'Each scan adds a second weight source to the order record', id="record", the five outputs, the boundary sentence and 'See a sample record in the demo') so it sits directly after the problem block and before 'How it works'. Recast its five bullets as a two-column table, 'Returned output | What it changes for the prescriber'. This puts value before mechanics, as the kit order requires, and closes the three-screen CTA gap after the hero.

points_lost.Proof of belonging to the vertical: GPhC is the only regulator named (no MHRA or CQC). The pharmacy's systems stay generic ('the pharmacy's system', 'review screen'). There is no anonymised vertical figure. The logo strip is mostly non-pharmacy clients (Burlington Medical, Warrior Consultants). The comparison never names the real alternatives: a scales photo, a video consultation, GP or SCR records.
points_lost.Claims discipline: The card heading 'Fewer follow-up requests' is an unhedged outcome with no internal figure. It also pulls against the FAQ's 'one part of the verification process'. The logo caption 'including online pharmacies' (plural) traces to one client only. The Feb 2025 guidance sentence ('has required ... weight, height and/or BMI') is a paraphrase sourced through the April 2026 review and is not linked to the guidance itself. BMI and GDPR are never expanded.
points_lost.Sales argument: 'How it works' sits before 'What you get' (the scan record), which breaks the value-before-mechanics rule. The H1 outcome 'a second weight source' is what FitXpress returns, not what the pharmacy pays for. The RTPV step and the Admin Panel line carry no spared or gained benefit. Two of the 'For patients' cards are pharmacy benefits or a patient burden (off-screen numbers, repeat photos at re-order). The strongest argument is left implicit: live in-SDK capture answers GPhC's 'easily manipulated photographs' concern, but no comparison row or sentence says so.
points_lost.Uniqueness against the parent: FAQ Q1 (GPhC weight verification) overlaps the hub compliance guide's topic. Overlap with the /for-bmi-verification/ feature page for the same audience is likely and cannot be checked from these inputs.
points_lost.Conversion: No CTA between the hero and the record block, which comes after patients, problem and how-it-works (3 screens). The record CTA is only a text link. Events are specced but unverified because the page is unpublished.
points_lost.Copy in the buyer's language: The lede opens with an imperative and no named subject ('Give prescribers...'), and so do the H2s 'Start with...' and 'See FitXpress...'. Insider terms are missing: consultation questionnaire, GLP-1, video consultation, SCR/GP record. The comparison's 'manually reviewed evidence' stays vague. US spelling (anonymized, authorization) on a UK-targeted page.
points_lost.Human copy: Clean but flat and template-shaped: every block runs eyebrow, H2, intro line, then a '→' link line. 'The pharmacy' appears 20 times and 'prescriber' 19 times in about 1,600 words. Sentence length is uniform at roughly 15-25 words. Three-item cadences repeat ('walk..., show... and scope...'; 'the order flow, a sample record and the integration pattern'). There is one real opinion line plus clear boundaries, which keeps it above 6.
points_lost.Search and AI visibility: The focus keyphrase 'weight checks for online pharmacies' is not in the H1 and is unlikely to be the main query. 'BMI verification', the dominant term in this vertical, is absent from the H1. FAQ Q4 ('How do scan results reach the prescriber?') repeats How-it-works step 3. The record is a bullet list rather than a quotable table. The GEO phrases cannot be verified against the keyword map.
points_lost.Place in the site and technical layer: No link up to a product page and no sibling vertical cards (fitness and insurance are not linked). Performance was not measured, no full keyboard tab-through was done, and 1440 px was not checked.
